words.gloss: bṛhatī (Solanum indicum, Indian nightshade; standard); kṣīrakākolī (an aṣṭavarga herb, identity disputed); pṛśniparṇī (Uraria picta; standard); śatāvarī (Asparagus racemosus, wild asparagus; standard)

hindi: बृहती यानी बड़ी कटेरी, क्षीरकाकोली, पृश्निपर्णी यानी पिठवन और शतावरी यानी सतावर।
english: Bṛhatī (Indian nightshade), kṣīrakākolī, pṛśniparṇī and śatāvarī (wild asparagus).
notes: GROUPING: a list of four drug names with no verb; 74 continues the list (kāśmarya and the rest), and 72 ends with 'nyagrodhādyaiś caturbhiḥ', so the list may belong to a group of drugs introduced there, but the text of 73 does not say what the drugs are used for. Identifications: bṛhatī = Solanum indicum (standard); pṛśniparṇī = Uraria picta (standard); śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus (standard); kṣīrakākolī is one of the aṣṭavarga drugs whose botanical identity is disputed and is left unidentified in the translation. 'kṣīrakākolī' could in theory be read as two items (kṣīra, kākolī), but it is a normal single drug name, so it is kept as one.

hindi: काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, बदरी यानी बेर, मूर्वा यानी सम्भवतः मरोड़फली, तथा उशीर यानी खस और प्रियंगु, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है।
english: Kāśmarya (gmelina), badarī (jujube), mūrvā (probably bowstring hemp), and likewise uśīra (vetiver) and priyaṅgu (identity disputed).
notes: GROUPING: continues the list begun in 73; no verb in the unit. Orthographic normalisation recorded once for this chunk: printed doubled consonants (-rvv- in 'mūrvvā', -rtt- in 'ārtta', 'nivarttayati') are given as -rv-, -rt- in `w`. Identifications: kāśmarya, badarī, uśīra standard; mūrvā probable (Marsdenia tenacissima; some use other plants); priyaṅgu disputed (Callicarpa macrophylla is the commonly given plant, but Aglaia and others are also named).

words.gloss: jīvādāna (lit. 'taking away of life'; a named condition, see notes)
ghee; añjana (a collyrium substance, kind not stated); joined with

hindi: जीवादान में, उबाले हुए दूध में, घी और अंजन से युक्त दो।
english: In jīvādāna, in boiled milk, two (ones) joined with ghee and añjana (a collyrium substance).
notes: GROUPING: 'dvau' (two) agrees with 'bastī' (dual) in 76, so 75 and 76 appear to be one sentence. 'jīvādāna' is literally 'taking away of life/jīva'; the text does not define it here. The animal milks and blood used in 77-79 suggest a loss of blood or vital substance, but that is an inference, not stated, and is not applied in the translation. 'añjana' is a collyrium substance; which one is not stated (71 also has añjana with honey and ghee). 'śṛte kṣīre' is taken as 'in (with) boiled milk'.

hindi: वैद्य को दोनों बस्तियाँ ठंडी, मधु और शर्करा सहित देनी चाहिए।
english: The two bastis should be given by the physician, cool, with honey and sugar.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 75 ('dvau ... saṃyutau'). 'śarkarā' is rendered 'sugar'; whether crystal sugar or another form is not stated.

hindi: गाय के भी, बकरी और भैंस के दूधों से, जीवनीय यानी जीवन बढ़ाने वालों से भी युक्त।
english: With the milks of cow too, goat and she-buffalo, also joined with jīvanīya (life-promoting) ones.
notes: GROUPING: 77, 78 and 79 appear to form one sentence (instrumentals in 77-78, verb 'praśasyate' in 79). The printed token 'go'pyajā...' is split go + api + ajā..., which gives two 'api' in the line (one inside the compound and one at the end); the metre is regular (16 syllables), so no change is proposed. 'jīvanīya' is the name of a standard group of life-promoting drugs; its members are not listed in this unit and are not supplied.

words.gloss: other; born; blood (read as: blood of other-born ones, uncertain)

hindi: खरगोश, एण यानी हिरण, भालू, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, बिल्ली, भैंस और अन्य से उत्पन्न के रक्तों से।
english: With the blood of hare, eṇa (antelope), bear (on a conjectural reading), cat, she-buffalo and other-born (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: 'dakṣa' is not an animal; 'ṛkṣa' (bear) fits the list of animals, and 'śaśaiṇarkṣa' (7 syllables) + 'mahiṣyanyajaśoṇitaiḥ' (9) gives exactly 16 syllables, while the printed 'dakṣa' makes 17 (ऋक्ष/दक्ष look alike in print)
doubtful: 'anyaja' ('other-born') is unclear in this list; 'ajā' (goat) would fit a list of animals, but it would make the line 15 syllables, so the printed form is kept and read literally

notes: GROUPING: 77-79 appear to be one sentence; the instrumentals here (blood, śoṇita) go with 'sadyaskaiḥ mṛditaiḥ' in 79. The word 'śoṇita' means blood; the list gives animals whose blood is meant. 'ṛkṣa' for the printed 'dakṣa' is conjectural. The last member 'anya-ja' is not clear ('born of others'); no animal is added. 'mārjāra' is cat.

hindi: ताज़े, मसले हुए से बस्ति जीवादान में प्रशस्त मानी जाती है।
english: With fresh, crushed (ones), basti is recommended in jīvādāna.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 77-78; the adjectives 'sadyaskaiḥ mṛditaiḥ' agree with the instrumentals of 78 (blood) and are left as '(ones)' here. 'mṛdita' may also be 'rubbed, mixed'; that crushing fits blood less well than the milks or drugs is not resolved. 'sadyaska' is 'fresh' (lit. 'of the same day').

words.gloss: snehana (oleating, oily) ones (conjectural; printed as ehanān)

hindi: अब सुकुमारों के ये मृदु निरूह और अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार स्नेहन।
english: Now, of the delicate, these mild nirūhas (decoction enemas) and, on a conjectural reading, snehanas (oleating ones),

text_flags.why: possible: 'ehanān' is not a word; 'snehanān' (oleating, oily) fits the sense (nirūha and sneha are the two kinds of basti) and the metre; the 's' may have been dropped in print

notes: GROUPING: 80 and 81 appear to be one sentence; the verb 'vakṣyāmi' (I shall state) is in 81, so 80 has no verb. 'sukumāra' is 'very tender, delicate'. The pair 'nirūha' (decoction enema) and 'snehana/sneha' (oily enema) is a reading; the printed 'ehana' is unclear.

words.gloss: by prasṛtas (a measure: a palmful, about two pala; standard)

hindi: और कर्म से पीड़ित हुओं के लिए प्रसृत यानी हथेली-भर माप के हिसाब से अलग-अलग कहूँगा।
english: And for those afflicted by the action (karman), I shall state, by prasṛtas (palmful measures), separately.
notes: GROUPING: continues 80; 'vakṣyāmi' governs both. 'karman' here probably refers to the evacuative procedures (vamana, virecana and the like) that have afflicted the person, but the text says only 'by the action'; the literal rendering is kept. 'viplutānām' is 'of those afflicted/harmed'. 'prasṛta' is a traditional measure (the hollow of the hand, about two pala; standard).

words.gloss: from oil and ghee (conjectural; printed as -naila-)

hindi: दूध से दो प्रसृत बनाने चाहिए; मधु के साथ, तेल और घी से तीन, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार।
english: Two prasṛtas are to be made from milk; with honey, three from oil and ghee (on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ddhau' for 'dvau' (द्वौ/द्धौ look alike in print); the dual agrees with 'prasṛtau', 'kāryau'

possible: 'madhunaila' is not clear; 'madhunā taila-ghṛtāt' (with honey, from oil and ghee) matches the ablative pattern 'kṣīrāt'; the metre of the half-line then has 9 syllables, so this is only a conjecture

notes: GROUPING: 82 appears to give the quantities of a basti whose churning with a khaja is in 83. The second half is uncertain. Another reading: three prasṛtas made up of honey, oil and ghee (one each). 'ela' (cardamom) is also possible for the printed 'aila', but no spice is added. Quantities are not applied beyond what is printed.

hindi: खज यानी मथानी से मथी हुई बस्ति वात का नाश करने वाली और बल तथा वर्ण करने वाली है।
english: The basti churned with a khaja (churning stick) is Vāta-destroying and makes strength and colour.
notes: GROUPING: appears to follow the quantities of 82. 'khaja' is a churning rod or stirring stick (standard). 'varṇa' is colour, complexion.

words.gloss: oil; prasannā (probably the clear part of a fermented liquor); honey; ghee

hindi: एक-एक प्रसृत, तेल, प्रसन्ना यानी सम्भवतः मदिरा का निथरा भाग, मधु और घी का।
english: One prasṛta each of oil, prasannā (probably clear liquor), honey and ghee.
notes: GROUPING: appears to begin a recipe that goes on in 85 (the decoctions and 'sa vātajit'). 'prasannā' is taken as the clear upper part of a fermented liquor (probable); the text gives no more.

words.gloss: bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos; standard); beginning with; roots; decoction
from kaulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard); the word 'decoction' is understood

hindi: बिल्व आदि की जड़ों के काढ़े से दो, कुलत्थ से दो; वह वात को जीतने वाली है।
english: From the decoction of the roots beginning with bilva (bael), two (ones); from kaulattha (horse gram), two (ones); that one conquers Vāta.
notes: GROUPING: continues 84 (the one-prasṛta items); the whole is one recipe. 'bilvādimūla' means the roots of bilva and the others; which others is not stated. 'kaulatthāt' has no noun: 'decoction' is understood from the first half (not added in the translation).

words.gloss: paṭola (pointed gourd, Trichosanthes dioica; standard); nimba (neem, Azadirachta indica; standard); bhūtīka (identity disputed); rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata; disputed); saptacchada (devil's tree, Alstonia scholaris; standard)

hindi: पटोल यानी परवल, निम्ब यानी नीम, भूतीक, रास्ना और सप्तच्छद यानी छतिवन के जल का।
english: Of the water of paṭola (pointed gourd), nimba (neem), bhūtīka, rāsnā and saptacchada (devil's tree),

text_flags.why: possible: 'samacchada' is not a plant name; 'saptacchada' (Alstonia scholaris) fits a list of five bitter drugs (see 88 'pañcatikta'); 'sama'/'sapta' look alike in print

notes: GROUPING: 86, 87 and 88 appear to be one sentence (prasṛta of each, ghee, mustard paste, the five bitters). The token 'paṭolaniṃbabhūtīkarāsnā' leaves 'saptacchada' in the second token, joined with 'ambhasaḥ'; the five items are paṭola, nimba, bhūtīka, rāsnā, saptacchada. 'ambhasaḥ' is genitive or ablative ('of/from water'); the text says 'water' and not 'decoction', and none is added. Identifications: paṭola, nimba, saptacchada standard; rāsnā probable-to-disputed (Pluchea lanceolata, with Alpinia galanga and orchid sources also named); bhūtīka disputed.

words.gloss: having a paste (kalka) of mustard (sarṣapa; Brassica species, standard)

hindi: एक प्रसृत अलग-अलग, और घी से भी; सरसों के कल्क वाली बस्ति।
english: A prasṛta, separately, and (one) from ghee; a basti having a paste (kalka) of mustard.
notes: GROUPING: continues 86 ('prasṛtaḥ' of the waters, separately) and runs on into 88; 'bastiḥ' is the subject of 88. The words 'one from ghee' are the literal ablative 'ājyāt'.

words.gloss: abhiṣyanda (lit. 'oozing, flowing out'); kṛmi (worms, intestinal worms; probable); kuṣṭha (skin disease, traditionally 'leprosy'; standard); prameha (urinary disorders, traditionally twenty kinds, linked to diabetes; probable); destroyer

hindi: पाँच तिक्तों सहित, अभिष्यन्द, कृमि यानी कीड़े, कुष्ठ यानी त्वचा रोग, जिसे परम्परा से कोढ़ कहा गया, और प्रमेह यानी मूत्र-विकार, जो सम्भवतः मधुमेह से जुड़ा है, इनका नाश करने वाली।
english: With the five bitters (pañcatikta), destroying abhiṣyanda, worms (kṛmi), kuṣṭha (skin disease, traditionally "leprosy") and prameha (urinary disorders, probably including diabetes).
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 86-87 ('bastiḥ ... sarṣapakalkavān'). 'pañcatikta' is the five bitters; the five drugs named in 86 may be meant, but the text does not say so. 'abhiṣyanda' is kept in Sanskrit (the sense is oozing or exudative congestion; for the eyes it is conjunctivitis, which is not stated here). Identifications: kuṣṭha = group of skin diseases, traditional rendering leprosy (standard); prameha = group of urinary disorders, associated with diabetes (probable); kṛmi = worms (probable).

words.gloss: viḍaṅga (false black pepper, Embelia ribes; standard)
triphalā (the three fruits: harītakī, Terminalia chebula; bibhītaka, Terminalia bellirica; āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica; standard)
fruit of śigru (drumstick tree, Moringa oleifera; standard)
ākhukarṇikā (= mūṣākarṇī; probably Merremia emarginata or Ipomoea reniformis; disputed); printed as ākhukarṇi-jāḥ

hindi: विडंग यानी वायविडंग, त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला, शिग्रु का फल यानी सहजन की फली, मुस्ता यानी नागरमोथा और आखुकर्णी, जिसकी पहचान सम्भवतः मूसाकानी है।
english: Viḍaṅga (false black pepper), triphalā (the three fruits: harītakī, bibhītaka and āmalakī), the fruit of śigru (drumstick tree), mustā (nutgrass) and ākhukarṇī (probably mūṣākarṇī).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ja' ('born of') after ākhukarṇī is unusual; 'ākhukarṇikāḥ' gives the fifth drug of the 'five decoctions' of 90 and has the same number of syllables

notes: GROUPING: a list of five drugs (viḍaṅga, triphalā, śigru fruit, mustā, ākhukarṇī) that 90 calls 'five decoctions'; the verb of the passage is in 90-91. 'triphalā' is counted as one item, as the count of five in 90 requires. Identifications: viḍaṅga, mustā, śigru standard; ākhukarṇī/mūṣākarṇī disputed (Ipomoea reniformis, Merremia emarginata and others).

hindi: पाँच प्रसृत काढ़े और तेल से एक, उन्हें मथकर,
english: Five prasṛtas of decoctions (kaṣāya), and one from oil; having churned them,
notes: GROUPING: continues 89 (the five drugs) and the nirūha of 91. 'kaṣāya' here is the preparation (decoction), not the astringent taste. 'one from oil' is the literal 'tailāt ekaḥ'; 'prasṛta' is understood.

words.gloss: vella (identity disputed; sometimes taken as viḍaṅga); pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard); paste (kalka); joined

hindi: निरूह बस्ति, कृमि का नाश करने वाली, वेल्ल और पिप्पली यानी पीपर के कल्क से युक्त।
english: A nirūha (decoction enema), destroying worms, joined with a paste (kalka) of vella and pippalī (long pepper).
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 89-90 ('having churned them, a nirūha ...'). 'vella' is left as the printed name: identity disputed (viḍaṅga or another drug).

words.gloss: payasyā (identity disputed); ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard); sthirā (probably Desmodium gangeticum; disputed); rāsnā (see 86); vidārī (Indian kudzu, Pueraria tuberosa; standard); honey; ghee

hindi: पयस्या, इक्षु यानी गन्ना, स्थिरा, रास्ना, विदारी यानी विदारीकन्द, मधु और घी।
english: Of payasyā, ikṣu (sugarcane), sthirā, rāsnā, vidārī (Indian kudzu), honey and ghee,

text_flags.why: possible: genitive plural 'sarpiṣām' as in 84 (ekaikaḥ prasṛtaḥ ... sarpiṣām); the printed 'sarpiṣaḥ' is a singular genitive/ablative

notes: GROUPING: the genitive list continues into 93 ('ekaikaḥ prasṛtaḥ bastiḥ'). Identifications: payasyā disputed (several plants share the name, e.g. kṣīravidārī or kṣīrakākolī); sthirā disputed (often śālaparṇī); ikṣu and vidārī standard.

words.gloss: kṛṣṇā (long pepper, pippalī; standard); from the paste (kalka) (conjectural; printed kalkau)

hindi: एक-एक प्रसृत, बस्ति, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार कृष्णा यानी पीपर के कल्क से, वृषत्व करने वाली।
english: One prasṛta each; the basti, on a conjectural reading from a paste (kalka) of kṛṣṇā (long pepper), makes virility (vṛṣatva).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kalkau' (a dual) has no sense here; the ablative 'kalkāt' (as 'kṣīrāt', 'ājyāt') or the nominative 'kalkaḥ' are possible, so the reading is not firm

notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 92 (the list of ingredients, one prasṛta each). 'vṛṣatva' is virility, sexual potency; the text says only 'vṛṣatva-kṛt'. The reading of 'kṛṣṇākalkau' is conjectural. kṛṣṇā = pippalī (long pepper; standard).

words.gloss: oil; gomūtra (cow's urine); dadhimaṇḍa (the watery part of curd); sour; kāñjika (a sour fermented gruel)

hindi: चार, तेल, गोमूत्र, दधिमण्ड यानी दही के पानी और खट्टी काँजिक यानी खट्टे किण्वित पेय से।
english: Four, from oil, cow's urine, dadhimaṇḍa (the watery part of curd) and sour kāñjika (a fermented gruel).
notes: GROUPING: 94 and 95 appear to be one sentence ('bastiḥ kavoṣṇaḥ ...' in 95). The noun counted by 'catvāraḥ' is not stated (prasṛtas, as in 82-93, is likely but is not supplied). Whether the four are one from each of the four items, or 'amla' stands apart, is not decided by the compound. gomūtra is read as cow's urine.

words.gloss: in one with ānāha (distension of the belly with obstruction of stool and wind)

hindi: थोड़ा गुनगुना बस्ति, सानाह यानी आनाह वाले में और मूत्रकृच्छ्र यानी कष्ट से मूत्र आने में, श्रेष्ठ माना गया है।
english: A slightly warm basti is considered best in (one) with ānāha (belly distension with obstruction) and in mūtrakṛcchra (painful urination).
notes: GROUPING: continues 94 (the four items); the basti of 94 appears to be the 'kavoṣṇa' one. 'paraḥ' is taken as 'best' (the alternative 'other' is unlikely, since 96 has 'anyaḥ'). Identification: mūtrakṛcchra = dysuria (standard); ānāha = distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind (standard).

words.gloss: by mild bastis; become dull, sluggish (jaḍībhūta)

hindi: मृदु बस्ति से जड़ हो गए में तीक्ष्ण, दूसरी बस्ति चाही जाती है।
english: In one who has become dull (sluggish) from mild bastis, another, sharp basti is desired.
notes: GROUPING: 96 and 97 appear to be one passage (97 has no verb of its own; 'iṣyate' is carried). 'jaḍībhūta' is 'become dull, torpid'; here, dulled in response.

words.gloss: urine (mūtra); bilva (bael); agni (fire; may be the drug-name agni = citraka, Plumbago zeylanica; disputed); salt; kṣāra; mustard

hindi: तीक्ष्णता, मूत्र, बिल्व, अग्नि, लवण, क्षार और सरसों से।
english: Sharpness, by urine, bilva (bael), agni, salt, kṣāra and mustard.
notes: GROUPING: elliptical; no verb (understood 'is produced/made'). 'agni' is left as 'agni'; it may be the drug of that name (citraka, Plumbago zeylanica; disputed) or fire; 'mūtra' is urine, the animal is not stated. 'kṣāra' is kept (an ash-derived alkaline substance).

words.gloss: in due time (lit. the time having come)
to be produced, to be made

hindi: पर समय आने पर दूध, घी आदि से मृदुता का विधान करना चाहिए।
english: But mildness is to be produced, in due time, by milk, ghee and so on.
notes: GROUPING: follows 98 (sharpness by urine and the rest); 'tu' contrasts mildness with it. 'prāptakālam' may also be read 'when the time has come'.

words.gloss: strength; time (season); region; sātmya (what suits by habit); constitutions (prakṛti)

hindi: बल, काल, देश, सात्म्य और प्रकृतियों को भली-भाँति अलग-अलग करके प्रयुक्त की गई बस्ति
english: The basti, applied after distinguishing strength, time, region, sātmya (what suits by habit) and constitutions,
notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues into 101 (the verb 'nivartayati'). 'sātmya' is what is agreeable or suitable by habit. 'kāla' is time or season; both fit.

hindi: अपने-अपने औषध-समूहों से अपने-अपने रोगों को निवृत्त करती है।
english: with their own respective groups of drugs, causes their own respective diseases to turn back (cease).
notes: GROUPING: completes 100; the subject is the basti of 100. Orthography: printed 'nivarttayati' is given as nivartayati (see 74).

hindi: गर्मी से पीड़ितों के लिए ठंडे, और सर्दी से पीड़ितों के लिए वैसे ही सुखद गरम।
